questions.question_text: What is the maximum payout from the South Dakota Real Estate Recovery Fund per transaction?
questions.explanation: The fund pays actual and direct loss up to $15,000 (SDCL 36-21A-104). That ceiling is also the fund's total exposure for one licensee's acts, so several victims of the same licensee share a single $15,000 pool (SDCL 36-21A-112).

questions.question_text: Before a consumer can file a claim against the SD Recovery Fund, what must they first obtain?
questions.correct_answer: A civil judgment against the licensee
distractors: A written complaint from the SDREC
An arbitration award from a mediator
A police report documenting the misconduct
questions.explanation: The fund is a last resort: the claimant needs a final judgment for fraud, deceit, dishonesty, or conversion of trust funds and must show diligent efforts to collect it (SDCL 36-21A-104). The verified application then goes to circuit court in Hughes County.

questions.question_text: Under SDCL 36-21A-102, what is the minimum balance that must be maintained in the Recovery Fund?
questions.explanation: The commission must keep $100,000 in the fund (SDCL 36-21A-101). If the balance falls below that at the end of a calendar year, every licensee pays a separate fee with the biennial registration to restore it (SDCL 36-21A-102).

questions.question_text: A licensee's misconduct leads to a $15,000 payout from the Recovery Fund. What happens to the licensee's license?
questions.correct_answer: Automatic suspension until the fund is repaid
distractors: No effect on the licensee's license status
The license is permanently revoked
Only a letter of reprimand is issued
questions.explanation: The license is automatically suspended on the effective date of the court order authorizing payment and stays suspended until the licensee repays the fund in full with interest (SDCL 36-21A-114). A bankruptcy discharge does not wipe out that debt.

questions.question_text: The SD Recovery Fund covers losses from which type of licensee conduct?
questions.correct_answer: Fraud, deceit, dishonesty, or conversion of trust funds
distractors: Any error regardless of the intent
Only criminal fraud-related convictions
Only breaches of a fiduciary duty
questions.explanation: The judgment must rest on fraudulent, deceptive, or dishonest practices or conversion of trust funds arising out of a transaction requiring a license (SDCL 36-21A-104). Honest mistakes and ordinary negligence fall outside the fund.

questions.question_text: A consumer sues a licensee on claims that could later reach the Recovery Fund. When must the commission be served?
questions.correct_answer: Within 10 days of serving the defendant
distractors: Only after judgment is entered
Within 30 days of filing the complaint
The commission is never served before a claim is filed
questions.explanation: Anyone commencing an action that may result in a fund claim must serve the commission with a copy of the summons and complaint within 10 days of serving the defendant (SDCL 36-21A-103). The commission may then intervene in the action.

questions.question_text: A buyer wins a fraud judgment against a licensee. What is the deadline for filing the verified application against the Recovery Fund?
questions.correct_answer: Within one year after the judgment becomes final
distractors: Within one year after the loss occurred
Within 90 days after the judgment is entered
There is no deadline once a judgment exists
questions.explanation: The verified application must be filed within one year after the judgment becomes final, or within one year after any review or appeal concludes (SDCL 36-21A-105). Missing that window bars the claim no matter how strong the judgment is.

questions.question_text: Beyond holding a final judgment, what must a Recovery Fund applicant establish in the verified application?
questions.correct_answer: Show diligent searches for assets and that collection fell short
distractors: Show that the licensee's license has already been revoked
Show that the licensee carried no errors and omissions coverage
Show that the commission investigated and confirmed the loss
questions.explanation: The applicant must show all reasonable searches and inquiries were made for the debtor's assets and that whatever was realized was insufficient to satisfy the judgment (SDCL 36-21A-105). A judgment alone does not open the fund.

questions.question_text: A consumer's judgment against a licensee was entered by default. How does that affect the Recovery Fund claim?
questions.correct_answer: The applicant must prove the fraud or conversion
distractors: The judgment still creates a rebuttable presumption of fraud
The claim is barred because default judgments do not qualify
The commission must retry the underlying case itself
questions.explanation: When the judgment came by default, stipulation, or consent, the applicant carries the burden of proving the fraud or conversion (SDCL 36-21A-107). A contested judgment instead creates a rebuttable presumption that the commission may challenge.

questions.question_text: The Recovery Fund lacks enough money to satisfy a claim the court has authorized. How is that claim handled?
questions.correct_answer: Paid in the order filed, with interest, once the fund is replenished
distractors: Divided pro rata among all claimants pending that year
Denied outright, leaving the claimant to pursue the licensee
Paid immediately from the commission's general operating budget
questions.explanation: An authorized claim the fund cannot cover waits: once enough money is deposited, the commission satisfies unpaid claims in the order they were originally filed, adding accumulated interest (SDCL 36-21A-113). Claims are not reduced or prorated.
